document: ET-8 measured constants — THE ONLY PLACE THEY ARE ALLOCATED (理's rule, nirai 11409)
the_rule: a bit, a port, a route, a table — anything two documents could both allocate — has ONE machine-readable registry and a checker that fails; a document CITES, it never re-draws. 理 applied it to the address tail; this applies it to the numbers this package re-uses across artifacts.
why_here: the controller cost appears in 4 files and the R2b bar in 2. Each was typed independently. If one is ever re-measured and the others are not, the package disagrees with itself silently — and a cost number is exactly the kind of thing a reviewer recomputes.

controller_tokens_per_episode.what: the MEASURED cost of the controller's candidate passes for the MEASURED system (k separate full-prompt passes, mean k = 4.97)
controller_tokens_per_episode.note: a CHEAPER controller would move every head point left and strengthen every frontier claim; R2c and R2d failing to find one bounds the package conservatively rather than weakening it

r2b_bar_tokens_per_episode.what: the pre-registered cost bar: 0.71 actions saved x 707 tokens per marginal action (OLS fit of tokens on actions over the base's 300)
r2b_bar_tokens_per_episode.note: the other two bases (458 mean/mean, 406 budget-12) are printed in the prereg beside it; 528.4 failed all three so the reading never depended on the choice

base_success_pct_budget12.what: the base arm's success on v3 seed 21's 300 at budget 12, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
base_success_pct_budget12.note: R5-Q's bar is stated against this number

base_tokens_per_episode_budget12.what: the base arm's mean tokens/episode on the same 300
base_tokens_per_episode_budget12.note: R5-E's compute target is derived from this and the controller cost

NOT_used_by.results/r5e.json: R5-E compares base@16 (9,234.2) against G@12 ALL-IN (9,194.1) and never cites the budget-12 base. The registry claimed it did; the checker caught that on its first real run, which is the point of having one.

bounds: These are MEASURED values on one seed, one model, one task set. The registry fixes where they are written down; it does not make them general.
The checker verifies that code files AGREE with the registry. It cannot verify the measurement itself.
